I like to replace the fiblary3 dependency which is not maintained anymore with a newly created library called pyfibaro.
See https://github.com/rappenze/pyfibaro.
The library is newly created from scratch, supports development with devcontainers, contains pytest's with code coverage and contains type hints in the code, so to maintain it should be easy in the future. Also github actions for running tests on PR's and to create a release and publish the library in pypi are working on the repository.
I tested the library and home assistant fibaro integration both with HC 2 and HC 3 so this change is already well tested.
I will maintain the library and I'm happy to add other people to the repository to work with me.
@graham33 should I add you as you already stated that you like to participate in #66466?
Anyone from home assistant which I can add to the pyfibaro repository?
The only direct runtime dependency of pyfibaro is the requests library.

In the PR #71542 there was a suggestion to use a fork of fiblary3 which was not accepted. Therefore I created a new library from scratch.

pr_comments:
Many thanks for your comments.
My idea was to keep the initial PR small, but you're right, doing the API better is a good argument to have some more lines in a PR.
I extended the API with many methods, especially for fibaro devices. The code in HA looks now much cleaner and the library is responsible to give a typed access to the API data.
I decided against using a library like pedantic in the pyfibaro library because the data conversion of most of the data can't be standardized so pedantic can not really help much in this task.
Doesn't each device type follow a specific model standard in the fibaro api?

Unfortunately the device type is handled quite differently in the fibaro API. Sometimes it is a device category and sometimes it is a specific hardware device. Therefore the integration has a fallback to base type and even a second fallback to some basic funtionality if the device type is not known.

Also fibaro does not provide a list of known device types.

Also it looks like the fibaro API does not use the same types for HC2 and HC3. For example the climate device in HC3 seems to be always made by one device whereas in HC2 climate devices need to be a composite of several fibaro devices.

So I'm not sure if we can improve that logic. We can for sure discuss if the list of known devices should be placed in HA or in the API library. But if we move it to the API library I would recommend to do that in a second PR.
@MartinHjelmare Can we proceed with this PR in near time? Otherwise I will backport the fix for #85212 to the old version.
I think we can proceed. I still think the design of the library isn't optimal but you know best what kind of limitations there are in the API.
@MartinHjelmare So do you then merge it into dev or do you have more things to review / optimize?
I'll need to review the whole PR. It's on my list.

Many thanks for your feedback, I rebased the branch so it is ready to be merged.
I will also remember your comments and create additional PR's to address the issues once this PR is merged.

review_comments: For the future, I'd recommend the library to raise a custom exception for this case.
Side note: We shouldn't set a manufacturer if it's unknown. Just set it to `None`.

Side note: It's weird that we set attributes for Home Assistant on the device instance that comes from the library. I think the Home Assistant entity features should be kept on instances that are defined in the integration in the entity platforms or in a common entity class.

Generally it's good to separate the entity interface from the device interface.
Is the `AssertionError` still raised in the library?
Side note: If the library will raise any exceptions itself, it's better to raise library specific exceptions for all cases.
